results.comment: As a researcher in semiconductor physics, I would like to point out a factual error at 9:13. Si is an indirect bandgap semiconductor, so in its pure crystal form it cannot emit light at all, rather, the transition of electrons through the bandgap results in a phonon (crystal lattice mechanic vibration). There are some very recent studies on Si emitting light, but it needs to be grown in a special hexagonal lattice. Other than that, great video, and I am very happy to see Derek exploring my favorite technology field! And the story of Nakamura is very emotional, it's a great example of success against all odds.
results.comment_focus_summary: Pointing out a factual error: silicon (Si) is an indirect bandgap semiconductor and does not efficiently emit light in its pure diamond cubic crystal; light emission requires phonon-assisted transitions or special hexagonal Si structures reported recently.
